title: Regulatory / utility evidence checklist
scope: 93-site Epoch AI Track 3 universe plus the registry's named large-load/project evidence universe
semantics: FOUND means a public source family or discrete record is ingested and linked; PARTIAL means public evidence exists but it is not site-complete; NOT_PUBLIC means the requested detail is not exposed in the cited public source; a source-family record is not itself a site match.

checklist.item: PUC/commission dockets for every major suspected site
checklist.coverage: Virginia and Georgia have substantial docket/project coverage; exact site-level dockets remain incomplete across the full 93-site Epoch universe.
Public transmission/service records are retained where disclosed; many customer-specific agreements are confidential or not published.

ERCOT Batch Zero materials, IESO connection-status records, AESO load contracts, Georgia large-load contracts and named utility service projects provide public evidence; not every site publishes the underlying agreement.
CAISO, ERCOT, IESO and AESO study/process records are represented; technical studies can be confidential and therefore cannot be treated as universally obtainable.
Virginia DEQ permit identities and other state/local permit records are already in the project ledger; certification coverage varies by state and facility.
Georgia PSC, Virginia SCC, Ontario OEB/IESO, Alberta AUC/AESO and utility filings are represented; no claim that every utility/customer filing is public.
Virginia SCC PUR-2025-00058 and Georgia PSC large-load proceedings provide explicit large-load/data-center rate and cost-allocation evidence.
Virginia SCC transmission cases and Georgia Power transmission project records expose project-level substations/lines and their large-load service rationale.
Public supply/contract evidence exists for named projects such as Georgia Power large-load contracts and several utility/service projects; confidentiality is retained where applicable.

Georgia PSC Docket 44280 contains recurring large-load contract filings, executed contracts and a September 2026 contract summary; Georgia PSC also identifies the Commission's data-center contract reporting framework.
Virginia SCC has public large-load rate-case materials and numerous data-center transmission certification cases; Virginia DEQ permit identities are also ingested.

ERCOT publishes a Large Load interconnection process and monthly status reporting at aggregate dimensions; the September 2026 verification/audit process creates an additional authoritative evidence layer, but customer-specific RFI contents are not generally public.

Alectra Vaughan MTS #6 has named data-centre customer capacity evidence, and OEB-filed planning material includes additional data-centre connection capacity. IESO provides the broader 2,074-record connection application universe.
AESO publishes current connection project reporting and large-load contracts; EPCOR and AUC materials provide utility connection/tariff/regulatory evidence.

site_completion_rule: For a specific Epoch site, mark a regulatory category COMPLETE only when a discrete docket/case/agreement/permit/study/service record can be tied to the physical site using public identifiers. Otherwise retain PARTIAL, NOT_PUBLIC, or NO_MATCH_FOUND.
current_epoch_rule: All 93 Epoch sites already have a connection-match disposition. This regulatory checklist is a separate evidence layer and does not replace the 93-site connection audit.

sources.provider: Georgia Public Service Commission / Georgia Power
sources.record: Docket 44280 — recurring Large Load Contract filings
sources.description: PSC filing 228337 is the September 8, 2026 Large Load Contract Summary filing in Docket 44280. The docket also contains multiple earlier 2026 executed-contract and filing records.
Current public contract-summary filing for Georgia Power large-load customers.
PSC document describing large-load contract reporting, data-center rate treatment and generation planning related to large-load growth.
PSC docket 44280 filing associated with Georgia Power's large-load incremental revenue filing and executed-contract record.
Georgia Power project page states the transmission project is being developed to serve a specific large-load customer; no project MW is inferred.
SCC identifies the case as the source of large-load customer safeguards, including the GS-5 class and minimum-charge treatment for large-load customers such as hyperscale data centers.
Dominion filing states the project is to serve two data-center customers in Chesterfield County and identifies the Bermuda Hundred Switching Station and related transmission facilities.
Dominion application proposes new 230 kV facilities in Stafford County to serve a data-center customer; customer name is not public in the cited filing.

sources.record: Ex Parte: Electric Utilities and Load Growth
sources.description: Commission technical-conference docket addressing forecasting and providing service to large-load requests; Dominion submitted a data-center practice statement.
SCC public index lists current data-center-related transmission cases including Doubs-Goose Creek, Firehouse, Golden-Mars and the Meadowville project.

sources.record: Issued Air Permits for Data Centers
sources.description: State regulator inventory of individual data-center permit identities, including operator/site names and permit numbers.

sources.record: Nodal Protocols — Large Load interconnection status reporting
sources.description: ERCOT protocol requires monthly Large Load interconnection status reporting with load zone, TSP, load type, submission date, requested energization, size range, status and co-location fields, subject to confidentiality.
ERCOT's current Large Load Integration page provides Batch Zero eligibility, verification RFI and interconnection-study process documents.

sources.record: Batch Zero Verification Requests for Information
sources.description: ERCOT announced the issuance of Batch Zero verification RFIs to interconnecting large-load entities conditionally included in the process.
ERCOT describes a joint ERCOT/PUCT data-center information request covering grid dependency, water, cooling, ownership and other site/community impacts.
Alectra public project page reports a data-centre customer maximum demand of 108 MVA for Vaughan MTS #6; the registry keeps MVA as reported rather than converting it to MW.

OEB-filed material identifies a Richmond Hill data-centre compound and states that 176 MW of total capacity was requested in the area; this is area-level requested capacity, not a single facility identifier.

sources.record: Application Status — all connection proposals with executed agreements
sources.description: IESO publishes the application-status universe and says it covers all connection proposals with an application package and executed required agreement; 2,074 records are listed.
IESO explains that technical feasibility studies are confidential and require an executed study agreement; public final technical-feasibility reports are not posted.

AESO publishes monthly information for all projects following the Connection Process, including in-progress projects with accepted System Access Service Requests, recently energized and cancelled projects.

sources.record: Large Load Projects / executed load contracts
sources.description: AESO states Phase 1 allocated 1,200 MW via executed load contracts and identifies P2936 GLDC Load (970 MW) and P3083 Keephills Data Centre Phase I (230 MW).
AESO modelling explicitly includes the two Phase 1 large-data-center loads totaling 1,200 MW.
EPCOR states the AUC approved the project on March 27, 2026 and describes a new substation, 240 kV and 72 kV transmission facilities and the regulatory approval path.

sources.record: Distribution Connection Service Terms and Conditions
sources.description: EPCOR's current service terms define load customers, points of service and interconnection facilities in Alberta's distribution system.

site_targeting.source_family_assignment: Every Epoch site should be queried against its applicable national/RTO/utility/commission source family before a site is marked NO_MATCH_FOUND.
site_targeting.method: Counted Epoch site records with at least one retained utility/regulatory/interconnection-style assertion in the current site evidence layer. This is evidence coverage, not proof of a formal docket for every site.
